Devil Fruit
Statistics

悪魔の実

Devil Fruit;

Devil's Fruit (Odex)
First Appearance:
Chapter 1
;
Episode 1
User(s):
Various people, animals, and objects
For the song "Akuma no Mi", see
Akuma no Mi (song)
.
Devil Fruits
are supernatural fruits that each grant a unique power when eaten, at the cost of removing the eater's ability to swim.
[
1
]
A Devil Fruit power can only be held by one individual at a time, but will reappear in a new fruit after they die.
[
2
]
In turn, no individual may acquire more than one power,
[
3
]
with only
one historic exception
.
[
4
]
Devil Fruits exist along three broad categories:
Paramecia
,
[
5
]
the most common, which grant a vast array of "superhuman" abilities;
Zoan
,
[
6
]
which grant the power to transform into animals; and
Logia
,
[
7
]
the rarest and most powerful, which grant the power to transform into a natural element. Each fruit has a unique appearance, making identification and documentation possible,
[
8
]
although there is at least
one known case
of a fruit being renamed and rebranded.
[
9
]
Scattered throughout the
world
, Devil Fruits are rare enough to be considered myths in much of the
Blue Seas
. They appear to be most common in the
Grand Line
,
[
10
]
having empowered many key figures among the
Three Great Powers
. This rarity, coupled with their abilities, make Devil Fruits highly sought-after; some specimens may sell for billions, and extensive efforts have been made to replicate their powers and mass-produce
artificial versions
for warfare. The scientist
Vegapunk
has performed the most extensive research into Devil Fruits and achieved many unnatural applications and replications of their abilities, but not even he knows their origins for certain.
[
11
]

Haki

Haki
Statistics

Haki
Debut:

[

Literal Meaning:
Ambition; Aspiration;
Drive; Vigor;
Domineering Spirit;
Will (to Conquer/Rule)
User(s):
Various living beings
Fighting Style Focus:
Willpower manifestation
Haki
is a mysterious power that allows individuals to harness their own spiritual energy for various superhuman feats. As this energy manifests from willpower, it is theoretically accessible to all living creatures in the
world
; the vast majority, however, are unable to use it, either because they are unaware of its existence or due to lack of adequate training to achieve mastery. Haki users are common in the
, rare in
, and virtually non-existent in the four Blues.
Current understandings of Haki define three distinct types, each tied to a different ability:
sensing others' spiritual energy to anticipate their movements
, producing a
protective coating of energy from one's own body
, and—for a certain group of "chosen ones"—
overwhelming the willpower of others
.
[
2
]
[
3
]
Haki and its users have underpinned many significant events throughout the series—notably,
Shanks
used it to drive off the
Lord of the Coast
and save a young
Monkey D. Luffy
's life.
[
1
]
The term "Haki" was first used much later when
Blackbeard
was commenting on Luffy's bounty in
Jaya
,
[
4
]
and was explicitly referenced during Shanks' visit with
Whitebeard
.
[
5
]
The underlying concepts of Haki were introduced during the
Sabaody Archipelago
and
Amazon Lily
Arcs.
[
6
]
[
7
]
The concept was clearly explained later on by
Rayleigh
to Luffy at the start of the latter's training on
Rusukaina
Island.
[
3
]

For the song of the same name, see

The
Grand Line
is an ocean route which wraps around the entire
Blue Planet
, south of the
North
and
East Blues
and north of the
South
and
West Blues
. It is separated from the Blues on both the north and south ends by the
Calm Belt
. The Grand Line is split into two sections by the
Red Line
: the first section is known as
and the second is known as the
.
Reputed as the "pirate's graveyard," the sea and the islands possess a vast number of unpredictable phenomena that are not seen anywhere else in the world, many of which make sailing extremely difficult. Additionally, the Grand Line is home to the world's most powerful people and groups, including the
Three Great Powers
. Only one group, the
Roger Pirates
, has managed to fully sail across the Grand Line, and this achievement is what caused their captain
Gol D. Roger
to be labeled as the "Pirate King".
The Grand Line serves as the setting of most of the series, with almost everything since the
Arabasta Saga
being set in it.

Marineford
was the island of the base of operations for
Marine Headquarters
, where now the
Marine Base
G-1
is situated. It is where former
Fleet Admiral
Sengoku
and the
Admirals
resided, along with many
Vice Admirals
and lower officers when they were not assigned to another base. The city surrounding Marineford was inhabited by the families of Marine soldiers.
It is situated near the
Sabaody Archipelago
and directly next to
Mary Geoise
on the
Red Line
. The only safe way to reach Marineford is through the
Gates of Justice
. However, after the Summit War of Marineford, the location of the Marine Headquarters base of operations was exchanged with that of Marine Base
G-1
, which was subsequently renamed
New Marineford
.
It was the main setting of the
Marineford Arc
.
